Cabo Verde — 13th-highest-population country with zero prior corpus presence. Researched via a dispatched Agent. A relatively strong Layer-1 finding for a small island state; Layer 2's AFRISTAT lead was a mere acronym-glossary appearance and deliberately not force-linked as a methodology edge. UPDATE 2026-08-13 (AF/G.23, municipal-tier round): the previously-dropped Lei n.º 79/VI/2005 (Lei das Finanças Locais / Regime Financeiro das Autarquias Locais) has now been located in full primary text (hosted by the Assembleia Municipal da Praia) and is minted below as cv-lei-financas-locais-79-2005, with verbatim formula text for the FFM/FMC/FSM transfer mechanism.

reports.title: Índice de Preços no Consumidor (IPC)
reports.publisher: Instituto Nacional de Estatística de Cabo Verde (INE-CV)
reports.description: Cabo Verde's national CPI. INE-CV's own "Índice de Preços no Consumidor – Síntese dos Resultados" report states the classification standard as "Classificação do Consumo Individual por Objetivo (CCIO)" — Cabo Verde's Portuguese-language name for COICOP — with a price reference year of 2018 ("IPC18") and monthly collection ("recolha da informação mensal"). Recent releases (titles confirmed via INE-CV's own site listing, not independently fetched due to JS-rendering) continue at least through January 2026, independently corroborated by Cabo Verdean press coverage of a 1.8% April 2026 inflation figure attributed to INE.
reports.cadence_note: Monthly; confirmed current through at least January 2026 via INE-CV's own release-title listing and independent press corroboration.

reports.title: Constituição da República de Cabo Verde (2ª Revisão Ordinária, 2010) — Artigos 230 e 233
reports.description: Cabo Verde is a unitary state organised into 22 municipalities (concelhos) with NO intermediate provincial/regional tier — the closest available fiscal-transfer tier is national-to-municipal. Article 233: "As autarquias locais têm património próprio e finanças autónomas, nos termos da lei" [Local authorities have their own patrimony and autonomous finances, under the terms of the law]. Article 230 separately defines autarquias locais as decentralised public entities with political, administrative and financial autonomy.

reports.title: Lei n.º 79/VI/2005, de 5 de Setembro — Regime Financeiro das Autarquias Locais
reports.description: UPDATE 2026-08-13 (AF lead-chase round, resolving AF/G.23's open FFM-rate caveat below): CONFIRMED the FFM rate remains 10%, NOT raised to 15%. The only law amending Lei n.º 79/VI/2005 since the 2019 15% proposal is Lei n.º 52/X/2025, de 17 de abril (Boletim Oficial I Série n.º 30, 17-04-2025; index https://boe.incv.cv/Bulletins/View?id=84886, download https://boe.incv.cv/Bulletins/DownloadAct?id=84886), enacted and in force since 18-04-2025. Its own text ("É alterado o artigo 6.º da Lei n.º 79/VI/2005... Artigo 32.º Norma revogatória — É revogada a Lei n.º 24/VIII/2013") shows it amends only Article 6 (municipal fee-charging powers, adding an exemption for electricity distributors that now pay a separate "renda especial") and revokes an unrelated law; it does not mention "FFM" or "Fundo de Financiamento dos Municípios" anywhere in its full 18-page text, leaving Article 10 §3 (the 10%-of-tax-revenue FFM formula, documented below) untouched. Corroborating context (not itself dispositive, since budget laws never restate the underlying percentage): the enacted FY2026 state budget, Lei n.º 69/X/2025, de 31 de dezembro (OE2026; Boletim Oficial I Série n.º 133, 1.º Suplemento, 31-12-2025; minted separately as cv-oe2026-budget in cv-leadchase-ffm-status.json), Artigo 13.º "Fundo de Financiamento dos Municípios", fixes the FFM at "5.387.079.168$00 CVE" for 2026 as an absolute amount only (standard budget-law drafting practice) — a figure consistent with, not contradictory to, continued 10%-of-tax-revenue math and with Olavo Correia's own June 2025 projection that the fund "ultrapassará os 5 milhões de contos em 2026" (quoted below). Both pending-revision instruments discussed below (the 2019 proposal to raise the rate to 15%, and the separate "novo Regime Financeiro dos Municípios"/"Lei de Base do Orçamento Municipal") remain unenacted as of the most recent primary statement located (governo.cv, 12 June 2025; see cv-g23-municipal.json's updated entry for the fuller quote) — that sweep of the 2025-2026 Boletim Oficial was not exhaustive, so a future round could still re-check for a later enactment. — Cabo Verde's national municipal finance law, distinct from the constitutional autarquias provisions in cv-constitution-autarquias. Full primary text located (AF/G.23) at the Assembleia Municipal da Praia's own document repository, after a prior round (AF/G.17) could only corroborate it via secondary sources. Preamble: "Por mandato do Povo, a Assembleia Nacional decreta, nos termos da alínea b) do artigo 174º da Constituição, o seguinte" — i.e. this law cites the Constitution's Article 174(b) (general National Assembly legislative-competence clause), NOT Article 230/233 (the autarquias-autonomy articles already covered by cv-constitution-autarquias), so no dependency edge is drawn to that node (see _dropped note). Article 1: "A presente lei estabelece o regime financeiro das autarquias locais." Article 10 creates the Fundo de Financiamento dos Municípios (FFM) and sets it at "10% do valor dos impostos directos e indirectos efectivamente cobrados no penúltimo ano anterior àquele a que o Orçamento se refere" (10% of direct and indirect state taxes — IUR, IVA, ICE, Imposto de Selo, Direitos Aduaneiros — actually collected two years prior), split "75% Para o Fundo Municipal Comum (FMC); 25% Para o Fundo de Solidariedade Municipal (FSM)". Article 11 sets the FMC's own internal distribution across all 22 municípios: "20% Repartidos igualmente por todos os Municípios; 50% Repartidos na razão directa da população residente de cada Município; 15% Repartidos na razão directa da população infanto-juvenil residente, dos zero aos dezassete anos, de cada Município; 15% Repartidos na razão directa da superfície do território de cada Município." Article 12 (FSM) targets poorer municípios via a fiscal-insufficiency/poverty formula ("CF = Pm*(Cni-Cmi)") and Article 12(2) restricts FSM eligibility to municípios "à luz dos critérios estabelecidos pelo Instituto Nacional de Estatística" — a real citation of INE, but of INE's poverty-statistics criteria generally, not of the CPI report specifically, so also not linked as an edge to cv-ine-ipc (see _dropped note). UPDATE (AF/G.23): a 21 August 2019 Council of Ministers press release on the Government's own site (governo.cv) states a draft bill would raise the FFM share "dos 10% atuais para 15%" and that "o FFM esteve 14 anos sem qualquer alteração, situação nunca antes verificada desde a Independência Nacional" — corroborating the 2005 origin of the 10% figure. A later governo.cv press release (12 June 2025), quoting Vice-Prime Minister/Minister of Finance Olavo Correia, states it remains "urgente aprovar ... o novo Regime Financeiro dos Municípios" — i.e., as of mid-2025 the government's own language still treats a comprehensive revision as pending, so the operative FFM rate cannot be confirmed at 15% rather than the original 10% text found on ampraia.cv; flagged as an open TENSE/current-rate caveat rather than resolved. The same June 2025 release states the FFM "respondeu por 32,8 M contos" of the ~42,6 million contos transferred to municípios January 2016-May 2025, growing at "4% ao ano" and projected to "ultrapassar[á] os 5 milhões de contos em 2026" — aggregate, not per-município, figures.
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational instrument (with at least one documented 2019 amendment proposal and, per a 2025 ministerial statement, a further revision still pending as of mid-2025).

_dropped.why: Cabo Verde acceded to AFRISTAT in 2002 (per this corpus's earlier af-grok-synthesis.json AFRISTAT history note) and INE-CV's own "Estratégia Nacional de Desenvolvimento da Estatística (ENDE) 2022-2026" document (hosted on AFRISTAT's own site) DOES name AFRISTAT — but only in an acronym glossary ("AFRISTAT — Observatório Económico e Estatístico da África Subsariana"), not in a substantive sentence describing an actual methodology relationship. Too weak to satisfy the branch's citation standard; not force-linked. The same ENDE document does contain a substantive sentence naming ECOWAS (CEDEAO) as a sub-regional funding source, but that is about project financing, not statistical methodology, so also not minted as an edge.

The same ENDE 2022-2026 document states Cabo Verde had NOT ratified the African Charter on Statistics as of 2022 ("Não ratificação da CAE pelo país") — recorded as a negative finding for future reference, matching the pattern used for Sudan and Comoros this same round.

SUPERSEDED 2026-08-13 (AF/G.23) — see below. A national Local Government Finance Law (Lei n.º 79/VI/2005, "Lei das Finanças Locais") was corroborated by two independent secondary sources (a UCLG country profile, and an "Estatuto dos Municípios" PDF) as establishing a two-fund municipal transfer mechanism (Fundo Municipal Comum, 75%, and Fundo de Solidariedade Municipal, 25%) — but the primary text of the law itself could not be located that round despite multiple targeted FAOLEX searches, all of which returned unrelated Cabo Verdean laws. AF/G.23 subsequently located the full primary text (hosted by the Assembleia Municipal da Praia, not FAOLEX or the Boletim Oficial's own site) and minted it as report node cv-lei-financas-locais-79-2005; the original secondary-source figures (75%/25% split) are independently confirmed correct by the primary text's own Article 10(4).

Lei n.º 79/VI/2005's own preamble cites the Constitution, but specifically Article 174(b) (the National Assembly's general legislative-competence clause: "a Assembleia Nacional decreta, nos termos da alínea b) do artigo 174º da Constituição") — not Articles 230/233 (the autarquias-autonomy provisions that cv-constitution-autarquias documents). Per this branch's standing rule against assuming a topical match constitutes the same citation, no dependency edge is drawn between these two nodes; recorded as a note only since no edge actually exists in the `dependencies` array.

Lei n.º 79/VI/2005 Article 12(2) restricts Fundo de Solidariedade Municipal (FSM) eligibility to municípios meeting poverty criteria "estabelecidos pelo Instituto Nacional de Estatística" — a genuine, substantive citation of INE, but of INE's general poverty-statistics criteria, not of the Índice de Preços no Consumidor (CPI) that cv-ine-ipc specifically documents. Structurally the same situation as the AFRISTAT-acronym-glossary near-miss noted elsewhere in this file: a real agency mention that does not correspond to the specific report already in corpus, so not force-linked. No edge exists in `dependencies`; recorded as a note only.
